cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Let Them Think They Won
cards.instruction: Protect someone’s confidence by hiding how much you softened the challenge, changed the terms, or withheld an advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. You beat me at chess. Take a photograph of the board.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why didn't you use your queen?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. I wanted to explore the rest of my team.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you go easy on me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You found the finishing move. Let the photograph remember that.

mechanism: A grades its chess pupil first mating success while disguising its deliberately unused queen to keep the win credible.
confusable: Not protecting A losing status: A keeps directing B toward pride in B actual finishing move and away from the softened opposition.
comparison: Unused in-game advantage versus withdrawn cake entry.
